sources.title: The International System of Units (SI Brochure), 9th edition
sources.institution: Bureau International des Poids et Mesures
claimsSupported: SI units and coherent dimensions
distinction between quantities, dimensions and unit conventions
sources.limitsOfUse: Does not validate AXM numerical behavior or game-engine policies.

sources.title: NIST Guide to the SI — Footnotes
sources.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
claimsSupported: conventional standard acceleration of free fall g_n = 9.80665 m/s^2
sources.limitsOfUse: The conventional value is not a claim that local gravity everywhere equals it; AXM retains 9.81 as a legacy rounded game profile.

sources.title: Chapter 7: Newton’s Laws of Motion
claimsSupported: net force and constant-mass acceleration relation
scope assumptions for translational Newtonian mechanics
sources.limitsOfUse: Teaching material is not independent validation of AXM.

sources.title: Impulse, Collisions and Conservation of Momentum
claimsSupported: impulse-momentum relation
isolated-system momentum conservation
impact energy loss and restitution framing
sources.limitsOfUse: Does not establish AXM material constants or validate its collision solver.

sources.title: Box2D Simulation Documentation
claimsSupported: fixed timestep and substep engineering guidance
damping approximation and timestep sensitivity
sleep as a performance mechanism
tunnelling and CCD distinction
friction and restitution mixing as engine policy
contact and impulse terminology
sources.limitsOfUse: Box2D policies are not universal physical laws and do not prove AXM correctness.

sources.title: Box2D Publications
sources.authorityClass: primary author and engine technical publications
claimsSupported: sequential impulses
constraint and contact-manifold implementation references
continuous collision references
sources.limitsOfUse: Techniques require AXM-specific implementation tests and bounded claims.

sources.title: An Implicit Time-Stepping Scheme for Rigid Body Dynamics with Inelastic Collisions and Coulomb Friction
claimsSupported: rigid contact, impact and Coulomb friction require explicit numerical formulation
contact-method claims require convergence and scope controls
sources.limitsOfUse: AXM does not implement the paper’s full formulation.

sources.title: ECMAScript 2025 Language Specification
claimsSupported: JavaScript Number uses IEEE 754 binary64 semantics
numeric and bitwise conversion boundaries relevant to replay claims
sources.limitsOfUse: Language semantics do not establish cross-runtime whole-simulation identity.

sources.title: NASA-STD-7009B — Standard for Models and Simulations
claimsSupported: model and simulation credibility requires intended-use, assumptions and evidence boundaries
verification must remain distinct from validation
sources.limitsOfUse: AXM is not claiming NASA qualification or compliance certification.

sources.title: Verification and validation benchmarks
sources.institution: Sandia National Laboratories / U.S. Department of Energy OSTI
claimsSupported: code verification, solution verification and physical validation answer different questions
validation evidence depends on experiments, metrics and uncertainty
verification and validation benchmarks need declared application relevance
sources.limitsOfUse: Does not validate AXM and must not be cited under the incorrect supplied title.
